teaching_card.title: Complex Numbers (Hard)
teaching_card.body: The imaginary unit i satisfies i² = −1, and a complex number has the form a + bi. Add and subtract by combining like parts, multiply with FOIL and replace i² by −1, and divide by multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate.
key_points: Powers of i cycle: i, −1, −i, 1 — reduce the exponent mod 4.
Conjugate of a + bi is a − bi; (a + bi)(a − bi) = a² + b².

screens.title: Powers of i
screens.body: i¹ = i, i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1, and then the pattern repeats. To find i^n, divide n by 4 and use the remainder: remainder 0 → 1, 1 → i, 2 → −1, 3 → −i. For √(−n), pull out i first: √(−12) = i√12 = 2i√3.

screens.title: Add, subtract, multiply
screens.body: Treat i like a variable, then simplify with i² = −1. Adding combines real parts and imaginary parts separately; subtracting distributes the minus sign to both parts. Multiplying uses FOIL; the last term bi·di = bd·i² = −bd joins the real part.

screens.title: Conjugates, modulus, division
screens.body: The conjugate flips the sign of the imaginary part only. Multiplying a number by its conjugate gives the real number a² + b², which is also the square of the modulus |a + bi| = √(a² + b²). To divide, multiply the numerator and denominator by the denominator's conjugate so the bottom becomes real.
key_points: Conjugate of 3 − 4i is 3 + 4i; their product is 25.
